subject: general
question: Which river originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Narmada River** originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau** in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**, India.
 
• It flows in a **westward direction**, making it unique as most rivers in India flow eastward.
 
• The Narmada River is often referred to as the **"Life Line of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat."**
 
• The river flows through the **states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat** before draining into the **Arabian Sea.**
 
• It is one of the most important rivers of peninsular India and is considered sacred by many communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of the Narmada River:**

 
 
• The Narmada River is a **rift valley river**, flowing between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.
 
• It is one of the few rivers in India that flows **from east to west.**
 
• The total length of the river is approximately **1,312 km**, making it one of the longest rivers in India.
 
• The river is known for its unique **marble rocks** at Bhedaghat, near Jabalpur.
 
• The river is a crucial source for irrigation, hydropower, and drinking water for the states it traverses.
 
 
 
• **Other Rivers Mentioned in the Options:**
 
 
• **Son River:** The Son River originates from **Amarkantak Plateau** but flows **eastward** and joins the Ganga River. Hence, it is not the correct answer.
 
• **Tapi River:** This river flows westward like the Narmada but originates from the **Satpura ranges** in Madhya Pradesh, not the Amarkantak Plateau.
 
• **Godavari River:** Known as the **"Dakshin Ganga,"** the Godavari originates from **Trimbak in Maharashtra** and flows eastward, eventually draining into the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance of the Narmada River:**
 
 
• The river is considered sacred and is often referred to in Hindu mythology and scriptures.
 
• The **Narmada Parikrama**, a pilgrimage where devotees circumambulate the entire river, is considered an act of spiritual significance.
 
 
 
• **Important Projects on Narmada:**
 
 
• The **Sardar Sarovar Dam** is one of the largest projects on the river, providing water for irrigation and drinking purposes.
 
• Other projects include the **Indira Sagar Dam** and **Omkareshwar Dam.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Narmada is one of the seven holy rivers of India, including the Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri.
 
• Its basin supports diverse flora and fauna, including some endemic species.
 
• Hydroelectricity generated from its dams contributes significantly to power generation in the region.
 
• The river is also a source of livelihood for fishermen and supports agriculture in its basin.
